root.name: Pterodactyl Defense
root.moves: 1. Nf3 c5 2. c4 g6 3. d4 Bg7 4. e4 Qa5+ 5. Nc3 d6

overview: Black delays ...cxd4 and fianchettos, then plays ...Qa5+ against the White centre of c4, d4 and e4. The queen eyes the e1-a5 diagonal and the c3 knight, pressuring the centre and the e4 pawn. White usually keeps the Maróczy-type centre, while Black aims for ...cxd4 or ...Nf6 and counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the centre with Nc3, Be2 and O-O
Exchange on c5 or d4 when the queen is offside

black_ideas.idea: Hit e4 and c3 with the queen and bishops

typical_structures.structure: Maróczy-like c4/e4 against c5/d6 with the queen on a5

character.notes: Hypermodern and double-edged, with the queen out early and a fluid centre.

structure.notes: An asymmetric centre in the Sicilian style.

sublines_that_differ.name: Modern c4 Pterodactyl
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 c5 5. Nf3 Qa5
sublines_that_differ.how: Reached by a different move order from the Modern Defense.

character.reason: Early queen and a mobile centre lead to unbalanced, tricky play.

structure.reason: Asymmetric Sicilian-like centre with c-file and d-file tension.

level.reason: Understanding the centre matters more than memory.

plans.reason: Black lets White take the centre and strikes from the fianchetto and queen.
